memory_release_publication_follow_up.status: Implemented and independently source-reviewed; new Rust execution remains held
memory_release_publication_follow_up.first_incorrect_transition: A private-memory release commit can finish its atomic batch and advance commit_seq, then suspend acquiring the exclusive database-file guard for logical exit. Without a decided-outcome receipt, rollback or Drop restores uncommitted allocation/overlay state over that already-replaced image; retry can apply the sequence twice. This additional defect is source-traced, not newly runtime-reproduced in this environment.
repair: Publish the complete memory image and retire transaction-local allocation/overlay ownership synchronously under PagerInner before awaiting logical exit.
Evict only the flushed page IDs before optional cache admission, so a capacity refusal cannot preserve an old fallback image. Legitimate freelist reuse remains enabled.
Retain a committed outcome and exit-pending receipt. Commit retry, settle_commit, commit_and_retain, rollback and Drop finish only the remaining exit.
Use the existing exact-handle DetachedTransactionExit and process-root ownership for abandoned exits; no speculative allocation rollback or old overlay restoration occurs after publication.
Distinguish a pending exit from a fault after an already-completed exit using the existing maintenance lease, preserving exact-once accounting and the existing Phase-C fault hook.
Keep publication, cache and unlock timing attributed to their actual operations. No performance result is claimed.
